chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ill-gotten gains (al-suh't) are of numerous varieties; among them are the earnings of the cupper when he stipulates (a fixed price), and the payment of the adulteress, and the price of wine. As for the bribe in judgment, it is disbelief in Allah the Magnificent.'

key_terms.السُّحْتُ: Ill-gotten gains or earnings from prohibited sources

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of ill-gotten gains (suh't) and the ruling on judicial bribery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi categorizes 'al-suh't' (ill-gotten gains) by citing specific commercial and social examples, such as the fixed wage of a cupper and the price of wine, to illustrate prohibited earnings. It notably elevates the severity of judicial bribery ('ar-rishwah') to the level of 'kufr billah al-'azim' (disbelief in the Great God), a distinction often highlighted by Shia scholars to emphasize the spiritual gravity of corrupting justice compared to other forms of illicit income.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The ill-gotten gains are of numerous varieties; from these are the earning of the cupper when he stipulates (a price), and payments of the adulteress, and price of the wine. So as for the bribe regarding the judgement, so it is the disbelief in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Magnificent’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from al-Jamuraniy from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamzah from Zur’ah from Sanaa ‘ah who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘There are many kinds of Suht (unlawful and filthy). Of such matters is income from cupping on the basis of a condition (for payment), payment for indecent acts of (sexual) relation and payment for wine. Accepting a bribe is however, disbelief in Allah, most Great.’”
